newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria's Assad pessimistic over Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Syria's Assad pessimistic over Mideast peace.

text.p: Syrian President Hafez al-Assad voiced pessimism over prospects of Middle East peace after talks in Damascus on Tuesday with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
"It is difficult for me to say there is hope (for the peace process) in light of the current situation," Assad told a joint news conference with Mubarak at the end of their meeting in Damascus.
"I don't think there is anyone who knows what is happening and could say there is hope...Everyday we get a new proof that there is no hope," Assad said.
But the Syrian president said Damascus was still committed to the peace process and wanted to make peace with Israel.
"In light of what we see and hear the best we expect is the continuation of the stalemate until there are new prospects," he said.
Assad said that he discussed with Mubarak the stalled Arab-Israeli peace talks and other regional and bilateral matters and that points of view were identical on all issues discussed.
Mubarak said the alternative for peace would be "dangerous" not only for one state but for all the countries who are taking part in the peace process.
